req.title: Return 405 for unsupported /players root method
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when using DELETE on /players/ (collection).

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-036 requires HTTP 405 when DELETE is issued against the /players/ collection root. The SUT defines DELETE only at /players/squadnumber/{squad_number}, not at /players/. Tests must: (1) confirm DELETE /players/ returns exactly 405 (positive case for the error path, which is the expected outcome per the requirement); (2) confirm that a supported method on /players/ (GET) returns 200, proving the route itself is reachable and the 405 is method-specific; (3) probe the boundary between the collection root and the parameterised sub-resource to ensure the 405 is scoped correctly. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting the exact status code integer 405, checking the Allow header content, and verifying that adjacent methods/paths return different exact codes.

tests.name: test_delete_players_root_returns_405
preconditions: No DELETE handler is registered for /players/ collection
expected: HTTP response status code is exactly 405
trace: R-PLAYER-036: system shall respond 405 for DELETE /players/

from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_delete_players_root_returns_405():
    r = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r.status_code == 405

test_delete_players_root_returns_405()

tests.name: test_delete_players_root_vs_delete_squadnumber_boundary
preconditions: Squad number 1 exists in the pre-loaded fixture
trace: R-PLAYER-036: 405 is scoped to the collection root only; the sub-resource DELETE must remain functional
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_delete_players_root_vs_delete_squadnumber_boundary():
    r_root = client.delete('/players/')
    assert r_root.status_code == 405

    r_sub = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/1')
    assert r_sub.status_code != 405
    assert r_sub.status_code == 204

test_delete_players_root_vs_delete_squadnumber_boundary()

actions: Inspect exact status code to distinguish 405 from 404 and 500

def test_delete_players_root_405_not_404_or_500():

    assert r.status_code == 405
    assert r.status_code != 404
    assert r.status_code != 500

tests.name: test_post_players_root_returns_non_405
actions: Send HTTP POST to /players/ with a valid player body using a squad number not in the fixture
expected: HTTP response status code is not 405
HTTP response status code is 201 (created) or 409 (conflict) — either proves the method is allowed
trace: R-PLAYER-036: POST is a supported method on /players/; must not return 405
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import json

client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)

def test_post_players_root_returns_non_405():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 99,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post('/players/', content=json.dumps(payload),
                    headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    assert r.status_code != 405
    assert r.status_code in (201, 409, 422)

test_post_players_root_returns_non_405()
